reason: 'He says he's tapping Ackley on the shoulder to say goodnight, and then he admits the whole thing was a lie.' No such scene is in the novel; Holden's Ackley scenes (ch. 3, 7) contain no confessed goodnight lie (LitCharts ch. 3 and ch. 7 summaries). The 'terrific liar' line leads into his lie to Mr. Spencer about the gym; the quote and 1951 date are correct.

'She drew a small dot after the half note, then counted: the note, and the dot, one-two-three, and the fourth beat of silence before the next bar began, and the bar was full.' The rhythm maths doesn't add up. The bar was one beat short, so the dot's extra beat should fill it with no leftover silence. And a 4/4 bar holding a three-beat dotted half is only full if a quarter note or quarter rest is written, not an unwritten 'beat of silence'. The injected fact itself is stated correctly.
